items.title: Venice Biennale hit by mass protests, historic strike planned for Friday

featured_image.name: In Venice, the World's Biggest Art Show Descends Into Infighting - WSJ

items.description: The 61st Venice Biennale has plunged into political crisis during its opening week, with mass protests, a jury walkout, and a funding cut by the European Union transforming the world's most prestigious art exhibition into a battleground over the participation of Russia and Israel.

items.description: Thousands of police officers have been advised to disable the bluetooth on their Axon body-worn cameras during raids and undercover jobs to avoid being detected and tracked, after Four Corners exposed a security flaw with the devices.

items.description: The man told the Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion he was embraced by the LGBTQIA+ community when he came out as gay as a teenager, but the experience was markedly different when he told loved ones of his religious conversion.

items.title: US strikes Iran after warships attacked in Hormuz

featured_image.name: Centcom denies claim US warship hit by Iranian missiles

items.description: The United States and Iran exchanged fire on Thursday as three U.S. Navy destroyers transited the Strait of Hormuz, marking the most serious escalation since the two countries agreed to a ceasefire on April 8. U.S. Central Command said it intercepted the Iranian attacks and struck back at military facilities inside Iran, while President Trump dismissed the retaliatory strikes as a "love tap" and insisted the ceasefire remained intact.

items.title: Live: 'Led by lunatics': US and Iran exchange strikes in Strait of Hormuz

items.title: Trump gives EU until July 4 to ratify trade deal

featured_image.name: Von der Leyen calls Trump in new u-turn on tariffs

items.description: President Donald Trump on Thursday issued a new ultimatum to the European Union, giving the bloc until July 4 — the 250th anniversary of American independence — to ratify a trade framework agreed last summer or face escalated tariffs. The announcement came after a phone call with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and hours after EU negotiators failed to reach a breakthrough in overnight talks on the deal's implementing legislation.

items.title: 'Completely unprecedented': ISIS-linked Australians charged with crimes against humanity
items.description: The ABC can reveal new detail about the alleged treatment of a Yazidi woman who says she was held captive in the home of ISIS-linked Australians in Syria, including two women who are now facing slave-related charges.

items.title: Iran reviews US peace memo as Trump threatens bombing

featured_image.name: Trump threatens Iran with bombs unless nuclear deal reached

items.description:
Iran said on Wednesday it is still reviewing a US peace proposal that could bring the war to an end, even as President Donald Trump renewed threats of military action against the Islamic Republic if a deal is not reached.

An Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson told the Iranian Students' News Agency (ISNA) that "the American proposal is still under examination by Iran, and once it is finalized, it will convey its opinion to the Pakistani side," referring to Pakistan's role as mediator in the negotiations.[1][2]

Trump, speaking from the Oval Office, struck an optimistic tone: "They want to make a deal. We've had very good talks over the last 24 hours, and it's very possible that we'll make a deal". But hours later, he issued a stark warning on Truth Social: "If they don't agree, the bombing starts, and it will be, sadly, at a much higher level and intensity than it was before".[3][2][4]

items.title: Saudi Arabia, Kuwait restore U.S. military base access after Hormuz standoff

featured_image.name: Saudi's pushback for US to use bases forced Trump's U- ...

items.description: Saudi Arabia and Kuwait have lifted restrictions on U.S. military use of their bases and airspace, according to The Wall Street Journal, removing a major obstacle that had forced President Donald Trump to suspend his "Project Freedom" naval escort operation in the Strait of Hormuz just days ago.[1][2]

items.title: Rubio meets Pope Leo XIV amid Trump-Vatican feud
items.description:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in Rome on Thursday for a high-stakes diplomatic visit aimed at easing weeks of tension between the Trump administration, the Vatican, and the Italian government. Rubio is scheduled to meet Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican's Apostolic Palace on the morning of May 7, followed by meetings on Friday with Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani.[1][2][3]

The visit amounts to a diplomatic cleanup mission after President Donald Trump's escalating feud with the first American-born pope rattled relations with two of Washington's most important partners in Europe.

items.title: Russia tells diplomats to evacuate Kyiv ahead of May 9

featured_image.name: Russia warns foreign diplomats they should leave Kyiv ahead of possible strikes

items.description: Russia's Foreign Ministry on Wednesday issued a formal warning to all foreign diplomatic missions and international organizations in Kyiv, urging them to evacuate personnel ahead of possible large-scale strikes on the Ukrainian capital tied to the May 9 Victory Day commemorations.

items.title: Trump hosts Lula at White House for tariff, minerals talks

featured_image.name: Brazilian President Lula and Trump to meet at the White House

items.description: President Donald Trump is welcoming Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to the White House on Thursday for a working meeting that spans tariffs, organized crime cooperation, and access to Brazil's vast rare earth mineral reserves. The encounter marks the first in-person bilateral meeting on American soil since Trump returned to office and the most consequential diplomatic moment of Lula's third term.[1][2][3]

items.title: NATO scrambles jets after drones from Russia crash in Latvia

featured_image.name: Nato fighter jets scrambled as drones from Russia crashed into Latvia oil  storage facility | The Independent

items.description:
Two drones entered NATO member Latvia from Russian territory early Thursday morning and crashed in the eastern Latgale region, with one striking an oil storage facility in the city of Rēzekne about 40 kilometers from the Russian border, according to the Latvian army.[1][2]

Latvia's Defence Minister Andris Spruds told national broadcaster LSM that the drones were "probably launched by Ukraine against targets in Russia," suggesting they may have veered off course — possibly due to electronic warfare jamming — before entering Latvian airspace. No casualties were reported.[3][2][4][1]

items.title: Saudi airbase threat forced Trump to pause Project Freedom

featured_image.name: Trump's abrupt U-turn on a plan to re-open the Strait of ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump's abrupt suspension of "Project Freedom" — the US naval operation to escort commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz — came after Saudi Arabia threatened to deny American military aircraft access to Prince Sultan Airbase and Saudi airspace, according to two US officials cited by NBC News.[1]

The revelation offers a starkly different explanation from Trump's public framing of the pause, which he attributed to Pakistan's mediation and "great progress" toward a deal with Iran.[2]
